name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Wyoming's R+23 partisan lean makes a Democratic win nearly impossible
Chuck Gray holds a massive fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Lisa Kinney
Prediction markets price Republican chances near 98%
Open seat removes incumbency effects but does not threaten party control
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean, Gray's dominant fundraising and outside support, and markets pricing the race near 98% Republican all point to a safe Republican hold despite the open seat. The Democratic nominee has raised almost nothing, leaving no evidence to move the forecast materially from the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or independent expenditure surge against Gray could tighten the race, though even a large shift would likely fall short of flipping the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Incumbent Harriet Hageman is leaving the seat to run for Senate, making this an open-seat contest rather than a reelection bid. Statewide official Chuck Gray enters as the heavy Republican favorite, backed by about $1.6 million in fundraising and substantial outside spending on his behalf.

Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000 with minimal cash on hand, and no outside groups are active on her side. Prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 98% chance of holding the seat, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The main question is the size of the Republican margin, not which party wins.
